title: Virtual Machines: series, sizes and what each one is for

videos.script: Choosing a virtual machine on Azure starts with one string, its size. This lesson is about reading that string, and choosing it well. {{lab}} First, the lab. Nothing in this course touches a real Azure subscription. You work with the Azure command line, the Bicep compiler and Docker, on your own computer. {{answers}} Some of Azure runs there, and most of it does not. Every section tells you which kind it is. {{name}} Then the names. Standard D2s v5 looks like a part number, and it is not one. The family, the vCPUs, the processor and the version are all written in it, one letter at a time. {{series}} The families come next. Each one pairs processor and memory in its own ratio. You will see what the compiler checks about a size, and what it lets straight through. {{sizes}} Sizes double, and so do their limits on disks. Some software is licensed per core, and a constrained size switches most of them off. {{burstable}} Last comes the B family. It sells you a share of the processor, and credits for the rest. For a machine that idles, that is a bargain. For one that does not, you will work out the hour its credits run out.
